overview: The two broad categories of components that make up an ecosystem — living versus non-living.
genZNote: Biotic: the living cast of characters. Abiotic: the non-living stage and props they perform on.

aspects.label: Nature
aspects.valueA: Living components of an ecosystem — organisms and their interactions.
aspects.valueB: Non-living physical and chemical components of the environment.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Plants, animals, fungi, bacteria, competition, predation.
aspects.valueB: Temperature, sunlight, water, soil pH, minerals.

aspects.label: Typical Influence
aspects.valueA: Interact with each other through predation, competition, symbiosis.
aspects.valueB: Set the physical conditions and limits within which biotic factors can survive.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: An ecosystem is formally defined as the interaction between its biotic community and abiotic environment together.
overlay.commonMisconception: Dead organic matter (like fallen leaves or a dead animal) is still considered part of the biotic-derived detritus pool, not purely abiotic, since it originated from living organisms.
